key_themes: Micron record Q3 earnings beat on AI/data-center memory demand
Oil price drop on US-Iran diplomacy lifts travel stocks, hammers energy sector
Wendy's meme stock revival on Reddit WallStreetBets short-squeeze campaign
Sunrun-Tesla-Renew Home 16 GW virtual power plant deal for AI data centers
Alphabet replaces Verizon in Dow Jones Industrial Average (effective June 29)

stocks.reason: Reported record Q3 FY2026 results after hours: revenue $41.5B (+346% YoY) and EPS $25.11, both smashing estimates ($35.1B and $20.39). Q4 guidance of $49-51B far above consensus $43.2B. Stock up ~15% after hours after falling 12% during the session.

Surged 25.7% (up 30-40% intraday, trading halted briefly) after Reddit r/WallStreetBets launched a Save Wendy's campaign targeting the stock's 23% short float. New CFO Steven Cirulis appointment added fuel.

Surged ~23% after announcing a partnership with Tesla and Renew Home to aggregate 16 gigawatts of flexible residential battery capacity, creating the nation's largest virtual power plant for utilities and AI data-center hyperscalers.
Fell ~15% despite Q1 revenue growing 92% YoY on strong AI inference demand. Selloff driven by margin compression: guided Q2 gross margin to 36-38% and FY2026 core gross margin to 38-41%.

Jumped ~9% as WTI crude briefly fell to $69.63/bbl on advancing US-Iran diplomatic negotiations easing Middle East supply concerns. Lower fuel costs benefit travel platforms and consumer airfare costs.
Rose ~8% alongside Expedia as oil prices tumbled on US-Iran diplomatic progress, reducing cost pressures for travel industry and boosting consumer travel spending outlook.
Climbed ~6% as crude oil prices fell sharply on Middle East diplomatic developments, cutting fuel cost assumptions for airlines. Delta Air Lines also rose ~4% on the same thesis.
Gained ~1% after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Alphabet will replace Verizon in the Dow Jones Industrial Average effective before market open June 29, 2026. Stock is up 10%+ YTD.
Set to be removed from Dow Jones Industrial Average on June 29 as S&P Dow Jones Indices cited its low share price limiting influence in the price-weighted index. Had represented only ~0.5% of index.
Rose ~3% after receiving price target increases from both UBS and TD Cowen analysts on the same day, reflecting continued bullish sentiment on AI chip design licensing demand.

Fell ~2.2% after reporting Q4 FY2026 on June 24: EPS $1.32 (beat $1.31 estimate), revenue $1.61B (in line), but slid on weaker-than-expected revenue guidance for the coming fiscal year. Launched WISE Workforce Intelligence Engine.
Reported Q2 FY2026 results: EPS $0.43 missed $0.45 estimate, down from $1.50 YoY, showing significant margin pressure in homebuilding. Revenue of $1.11B narrowly beat. Shares active as midday mover.

Fell 3%+ as WTI crude dropped to $69.63/bbl on US-Iran diplomatic developments signaling potential reopening of oil flows. Halliburton and ConocoPhillips also fell 3%+ with the broader energy sector down 2%.
Upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight by Wells Fargo with a $33 price target (from $31) on June 24, citing improved risk-reward in single-family rental REITs as rate expectations shift.
Upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight at Stephens with price target raised to $45 (from $33), a 36% increase, reflecting growing conviction in data security demand driven by AI data sprawl.
